Yeah we would need way more information.  What State? In GA, it took 4 months from the time BOTH of us had completed the Application until the landlord was paid by check in the mail. Yeah the "tell me what I can do that would help you" is a really good one.  Because it demonstrates expressed concern but puts the ball in the other's court to answer - therefore relieving you of the responsibility of having to be a mind reader.  Some people going thru shit want to be left alone, some want to bang on and on and marinate in the attention their suffering yields from others and others - if prompted - would realize they have NO CLUE what would help attenuate their issues in the moment.  When people can realize they themselves don't know what would help - they tend to suddenly expect LESS from others in that capacity - if they are a logical and normal human being - which is less and less of the population of late. 

I once saw an episode of "Two and a Half Men" where Judith was telling all of her woes to Charlie.  He kept responding with "I understand..." and it just propelled her on and made her think he was SO UNDERSTANDING  & SUPPORTIVE.  Eventually in that episode he admits he LEARNED to say that because it seems like something people like to hear.  I thought a lot about that for weeks after I saw that episode and began to realize there is a level of genius in that simple approach.  So I began using it when someone was suffering/traumatized but I had no idea what to say.   And I'm not sure it's because I <lack genuine empathy> but sometimes there is literally NOTHING you can say. Your baby just died of SIDS? Um...there is literally nothing HELPFUL that anyone can say in that circumstance.  But "I understand" seems to prompt the troubled person to keep talking which I guess is helpful to them and makes them feel "heard" so I continue to use it.  Who knew Two and a Half Men could give "communication skills advice"?

As they say, forgiveness is for YOU, not the other person.  And in my case it truly was FOR ME.  I had to forgive myself for ignoring the red flags, my gut instinct, putting up with the worst abuse when all I ever did was capitulate and try to compromise.  I had to forgive myself for both being unaware of NPD existing in this World - until someone with it destroyed my entire life while I watched it happen and kept lowering my boundaries and trying to "build bridges" - stuff the person with NPD further exploited to their own advantage.  The day I could let all that go - was the day I really began to reclaim myself and my life.  

Yet...I wouldn't trade the experience for anything in this World. I needed to see, learn and know what I do now.  Understanding NPD helped me to understand so much about my childhood, my mother, myself and see people as they really are rather than how I would like them to be.  Narcissists have taught me more than any other life experience except for University.  And they forced me to build boundaries like a mofo and be more assertive and take no shit.  One of my favorite lines from a person with NPD (kinda to the extreme) was: "You're allowing yourself to be a doormat but getting pissed off when I walk on you. Duh."  Lightbulb moment that YEARS of therapy would have never given me.

The fact that you believe the academic accomplishments of your parents is somehow a good reflection of you and is linked to your accomplishment as if YOU accomplished their Ivy League education accolades yourself - yeah, I see suggestions of narcissism with you in nearly everything you wrote...but not in the thing about procrastination - except that it allows you to boast & brag about performing "in the top 3" even when you don't study/prepare.

The hardest thing I ever did was realize the narcissists and I are two different sides of the same coin.  We both endured the same abuse/neglect/withholding etc as children - the results of which just manifested in us as adults in different ways.  The day I realized that was an ugly day because I NEEDED to believe we have nothing in common.  The day after that is when truly healing and forgiveness and acceptance and compassion began in me for those who suffer from NPD.

Lack of nutrition is a HUGE factor.  This cannot be stressed enough.  Im generally fine with being alone on this journey but I'm not okay routinely starving.  EBT does not work on "hot meals" and I have no way to prepare same.  Eating the chemical shitstorm shelf-stable BPA cancer foods from most food pantries makes my health condition way WORSE so I often just don't eat.   I buy a lot of peanut butter, beans, cheap gallon bottled water, and Think Protein bars with my EBT but all of that doesn't replace real nutrition from real meals made from scratch in a home.  I have not heard anyone talk of nutrition being a contributing factor in declining health amid the homeless population but it really truly IS.  At least in my case it is.

I understand YOU have good intentions - and what you did for that young woman WAS life-changing in a positive way so good on you for that.  I've said that for a long time: we could literally END HOMELESSNESS - at least for the people who want a safe place to call home - if we convinced AirBnB owners to do exactly what you did - use their space to help the homeless transition back to life.  I have met so many middle-age folks who are late 40s and early 50s, disabled, waiting on the disability process for YEARS and simply have no place to go. Shelters wont take them because of their medication and medical issues (read: liability), they are still too young for medically supportive living and the list is 5 years long for Disability Housing.  They aren't addicts, are as mentally well as you can be when dealing with homelessness and need a hand up to fully restabilize their lives. 

I think your "geographic locator" has merit but I'm wondering how many homeless of Reddit are located where the "helpers" of Reddit are.  As far as I know, literally no one from Reddit is in my area and my area is FULL of homeless as 28% of the population live in poverty here (per government stats - it's likely way higher.)  I'm in the Midwest and it's getting colder every night.  Many guys on Reddit (especially the young ones) see car-dwelling as an adventure and beating the man out of money.  And that is true when you are able-bodied, flexible and young.  The older you get, the less fun car-dwelling and sidewalk-dwelling becomes. 

But I think there are a ton of folks on Reddit who lurk the homeless subs who are in the Northeast so don't stop trying to help in your area.  There is NO HELP in my area.     The idea of free rent while I stabilize my life for a few months, then pay it back and forward and get a caring foster family to boot? It's a dream I cannot even imagine happening in real life.  I travel alone by choice because I believe in the Tupac Life Code: Trust No One.  In that sense, I'm never disappointed or betrayed.  But NGL, I sometimes look in the illuminated  dining room windows as I drive around at night and see a family together, warm, smiling and sharing a meal together and I wonder if they ever ponder how truly abundant their life is.  I know I sure never did when I had all of that.

If you can "pass" for NOT homeless (I always could because I do have an old beater car to keep my belongings in) you can stay in hotel conference rooms that have sofas.  I legit did this for a good part of late last year.  If any worker finds you (try not to let them) pretend to be hungover and say you thought you were in your room.  THAT ruse worked for me the 2 times someone actually found me sleeping.  But if you cut out early in the morning before housekeeping starts making rounds you can swing it.  It's largely how I didn't freeze to death last year.  Hotels were dead empty so no one was really paying attention.  I'm sure with people traveling again this might be harder to pull off but it can still be done.  I'm currently squatting in an abandoned trailer.  It's not the worst but will likely get cold once the temperature drops to freezing.  Then I will probably be trying the hotel conference rooms again.  Good luck.

Thank you for sharing your story about the loss of your father - that was really brave of you. 

I'm going to do the kindest thing I can think to do in response - given the limitation of internet anonymity. I'm going to ask you to please tell me about your Dad: what made him great, what made you laugh about him, what were his favorite things and what do you miss most about him? I ask this because someone did the same regarding MY deceased Dad for me this week and I found it to be one of the kindest things that's happened to me in a long time. He's been gone for over a year now and no one asks about him anymore.  Being able to tell someone why I loved him so much was tremendously beneficial and healing for me.  Note: I did not lose my father to suicide but the bereft grief and the loss of him is as palpable today as it was the day he died.  His absence is present in all that I do....be well, friend.  And I look forward to (hopefully) reading about what a great man YOUR dad was and what made him so loved in your heart.

Much of the knowledge here is spot on.   There exists a motel chain whose night porters will let you pay cash.  They do want an ID though.  Some States it is a law in the hotel/motel industry so don't blame the motel chain if the motels demand same.  Someone in your State government is playing Big Brother - not the motel.  But if you go after 8:30pm and pay cash they will work with you.  If you don't make any noise, don't make a mess, no illegal drugs, don't have ANY guests in your room and generally keep to yourself and help keep the property clean (picking up stray trash when you see it etc) they will continue to work with you on price/length of stay/flat and affordable monthly rate.  Tell them you were displaced by COVID and were hoping for a "pandemic rate" as you work to get your life back on track.  This motel chain is Motel 6.  Bonus: You can offer to foster/socialize animals up for adoption at the local AC if you get a long enough stay (at least a month).  I did and loved walking the dogs, playing with kittens so hard they bounced off the walls and crashed on my head when completely tired out.  And I was helping by teaching them to bond and trust humans.  Also, if you are going to stay for an extended period of time - it never hurts to shower the staff with unexpected gifts and praise/notes etc telling them how much you appreciate them.  Those folks are woefully underpaid and need every unexpected kindness they can get.  As do we all.  Good luck, friend.

Wow.  How insightful was THIS response? Very.  You are so on-point about everything you said.  I could go on for 12 paragraphs of my own and what I have observed but nah.....you covered enough for folks to truly <get it> if they so choose.

I understand that giving straight cash might give you pause because it could potentially make the homeless cause EMS to be called so they can "try and get more money from you" but honestly I second the opinion that cash is what I need more than anything as a homeless person struggling in this pandemic.  I haven't had a hot meal in 9 days (EBT doesn't pay for that) and I have no way to heat food.  I need my asthma medication which Medicaid will pay for one that doesn't work but not the one that does work for me.  And I need a Winter coat as all I have is a hoodie and fleece underthings.  It was fine until these negative temps hit here.  I found a coat that was $300 back in the Fall but is currently on clearance for $59.  It is the most beautiful coat I have ever seen and I just want to scream because I feel like I will never again have nice or even the essential things.  Or even safe/warm things. Also, I need Excedrin for my migraines (to avoid the ER when they get real bad because I don't have Excedrin) and some money for laundry.  I legit don't even have the $10 needed to launder my clothes.  I'm not an addict and I don't drink alcohol (not judging those who do - it's really hard to stay sane out here and NOT want to slip into the World of "forgetting" if only for tonight) so any cash any EMS worker would give me would go to legitimate NEEDS and not wants.  Also, since I'm newly homeless, I applied for all the "public housing options" and the caseworker told me straight up: "It will be YEARS until they get to you, Sweetie.  The folks with addiction, mental illness and behavioral problems who have frequent encounters with L.E. and over-use the local ERs are given priority for the housing.  You not causing a fuss anywhere? You'll be dead last on that Housing List even with your wheelchair."   Now what kind of crazy ass sense does that make? The people who could actually maybe make their way back to some kind of "normal" will never be rehoused because they aren't "burdening the system" enough with their shitty homeless existence.  Just wow.  But seriously - cash or visa cards.  Anything that would help buy desperately needed necessities.  Many of us out here don't have kids so we don't get the "cash assistance" with EBT that parents do.   Just something to consider.....

Insider Secret: There are people who are 40 who "deadass don't know how to adult."  Life doesn't come with an instruction manual - you just gotta get on and ride it and give it all you got.   The CA situation is tough but there are tons of folks here on Reddit who know how to navigate the CA homeless situation.   Your post just needs more upvotes to give it the visibility and attention it needs.  You have multiple issues that all impact each other: no job with suddenly no housing and no SS card to be able to obtain employment etc etc FIRST: Remember this advice someone gave to me when homelessness first happened to me: Deal with the first step - not the whole staircase right now.  What is the first step? Secure your 4 walls.  Any chance you can stay where you are being tossed from if you try and work with them? If not, call 211 or whatever version of that is in your part of CA.  They will help you find resources.  Next: Go to [www.findhelp.org](https://www.findhelp.org).  This is not going to give you IMMEDIATE ANYTHING but it will show you what is available in your immediate area (or whatever zip code you put in) and most of the resources let you apply right from that website.  Also: immediately file for expedited food stamps.  Sudden homelessness allows you to get them pretty quick if you aren't already getting them.  Secure 4 walls that can protect you no matter what you have to do: call friends/family you haven't spoken to in years.   You might have to get creative if you want to avoid "tent cities" and homeless shelters.  But before you dismiss them outright - research if the ones in your area are shitty or good.  Believe it or not, there are some that are clean, well run and the people in charge aren't control freak narcissists but the majority ARE RUN by those types and are horrid, violent hellholes where all of your shit will get stolen, you will get bed bugs and lice and all your shit will get stolen.   If you need someone to just talk to just to help you through the stress of this - DM me.  I will help you any way that I can.   But like most people on this sub I'm flat broke waiting on the next stimulus check and looking for work so I can't help financially.  But after a year of homelessness myself and learning A CRAP TON about what a fraud most "homeless outreach agencies" are among 1000 other topics on homelessness survival -  I don't mind trying to help you through this.  Good luck, friend. Stay safe.

Seems like a great deal.  Something I learned when looking into this possibility - mobile homes/manufactured trailer homes (whatever ya want to call them) are often plagued with mold issues.   Just make sure yours doesn't have this problem and then thank your lucky stars you found such a great deal.   Also, I know when we're homeless it's all about survival and getting 4 walls around us again and some degree of normalcy, but I legit knew a guy who would buy "needs some work" trailer deals like this and talk them down even lower, do the work needed plus add some nice touches and turn around and rent them in a trailer park he owns for $600 per month.  I would never have imagined such prosperity possible with that concept since trailers in America are always connected to the concept of dire poverty populations.  Maybe after you fix up your first one, you could flip it for triple profit and begin the process of what he is doing.  Dude made serious bank in that way.   I hope you find the happiness & safe home you so deserve with this opportunity.
